Loss of normal flat morphology. DMSO: spread, distinct red cortical F-actin stress fibers at periphery and faint green filamentous tubulin network. Treated: rounded, no spread lamellae; red and green condensed into bright yellow/white perinuclear cloud.

Actin texture high variance/contrast: patchy, heterogeneous bright vs dim areas; DMSO more uniform low-std.

reflection.text:
I was wrong: I submitted Microtubule stabilizers p=0.71, truth was Actin disruptors (cytochalasin D). Review approved this, but approval did not make it correct.

What the data did get right:
We correctly detected a strong, dose-dependent cytoskeletal phenotype. From 0.1 to 10 uM, act_std z went +25.9 -> +66.9 -> +139.0 -> +179.3 and tub_glcm_contrast z went +38.5 -> +138.7 -> +185.2, with tub_mean rho=+1.00 (p=0) and frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 (p=0), plus nuc_solidity z=-78.3 at 0.1 uM and cell loss toward 112 cells at 10 uM. That was a real perturbation, not noise, and monotonic across 4 independent wells.

What misled me and why:
1. Wrong mental model for actin disruptors: I coded e10 (tub_mean up) and e11 (act_std up rho=+1.0) as contradicting Actin disruptors in hypothesis_history step 16, expecting actin disruptors to decrease actin intensity/variance. In fact cytochalasin D caps barbed ends and can aggregate actin without net depolymerization PMID 6893622. That title alone in this run explains why act_std and act_glcm_contrast z +50 -> +138 -> +179 is consistent with primary actin disruption as clumps/foci increasing variance/contrast, not a decrease. I had no paper to support act disruptors -> secondary tubulin increase (search returned 0 hits), so I treated the huge tub_glcm_contrast z=+185.2 in e3 as stabilizer bundling.

2. Overweighting visual description and underweighting atlas: describe_phenotype e4 returned candidates: Microtubule stabilizers with 8 observations of lower density/rounding. I promoted that to key evidence e4 in the conclusion, even though it was based on 3 fields and summary was truncated. In contrast compare_to_reference_atlas e5 directly flagged Actin disruptors 3/10 k-neighbours at 2 wells, and e8 still had Actin 1/10 at 4 wells with Eg5 5/10 and Cholesterol-lowering 3/10. I listed e5 as the only supporting evidence for Actin 0.05 and kept Cholesterol 0.05 at 2/4 NSC vote, dismissing the split vote as atlas similarity rather than a signal my model was confused.

3. Misreading tubulin as specific: I used e10 tub_mean rho=+1.0 up to z 30.8 to exclude destabilizers and to favor stabilizers over Eg5, reasoning Eg5 should not increase interphase tubulin polymer. That is true for Eg5 vs stabilizer, but not specific: actin disruption forces cell rounding/compaction and microtubule-tubulin crosstalk, which also raises tub mean/texture by concentrating tubulin and promoting bundling appearance. Same for act_std/tub_glcm_contrast co-rising. I had no acquisition to disambiguate.

4. Acquisition choices amplified this: list_available_experiments e1 offered 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, 4 replicates. I sampled only the upper half: 0.1 (e7), 0.3 (e2), 1.0 (e6), 10 uM (e3), all single reps, no DMSO well of my own and left 4 wells unused. Starting at 0.3 and 10 uM saturated the phenotype (z +66 -> +179) and I never saw the low-dose onset where actin fragmentation/irregularity (nuc_solidity -78.3 at 0.1 uM already very strong) precedes secondary mitotic-like rounding. Single-replicate Spearman rho=+1.0/-1.0 over n=4 gave p=0 (e9,e10,e15) and I treated it as high confidence; review noted the same mitigation, but n=4 can still be perfectly monotonic by chance across correlated texture features.

5. Missed contradictory clue in e15: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-1.00 (p=0) I used to rule out Aurora (with e13 nuc_area rho=-0.80). Primary actin disruptors blocking cytokinesis should tend to increase multinucleation, as shown for cytochalasin B PMID 9568120 and actin polymerization/cell movement effects PMID 2995097, PMID 1176915. A strongly negative rho should have questioned my proxy or my model, not just confirmed Aurora exclusion. I also saw dose-response e12 cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 consistent with toxicity for any moa and did not weight it.

6. Structure lookup gave no leverage: e18/e21 returned PubChem CID 5458428 ChEMBL CHEMBL260287 mechanisms: none curated (name only (the BBBC021 structure is not in PubChem)). I had no chemogenomic prior to correct the imaging misinterpretation.

In hindsight, probability 0.71 was overconfident given 2/4 NSC vote for Cholesterol-lowering and 5/10 Eg5 neighbors. A correct update would have kept Actin disruptors much higher because the strongest features were actin texture (act_std +179, act_glcm_contrast +138) co-equal with tubulin texture, with extreme actin variance more parsimoniously explained by actin capping/aggregation PMID 6893622 than by secondary rounding alone, and the microscopist call did not include actin-specific filament imaging.

Next time for screening data: sample the full dilution series down to 0.003 uM with DMSO replicate, do not use tub_mean/tub texture increase alone to call stabilizer without orthogonal polymerization or p-HH3 spindle morphology, and expect actin disruptors to increase act_std/glcm_contrast via foci. This is a cell-biology screening reflection, not clinical advice.

Correctly excluded microtubule destabilizers (tubulin falls) and flagged nuclear/cell count trends (nuc_solidity -78.3, cell_count rho -0.80).
what_was_wrong: Called tub_mean/texture increase specific for Microtubule stabilizers; same rise occurs with actin-driven rounding/compaction.
Treated act_std increase as contradicting actin disruption, when cytochalasin D does not produce net depolymerization PMID 6893622 and increases variance via aggregates/clumps.
